### What this deck argues

It starts from a sentence someone said in the room: *"I just want to grasp
basic concepts and not feel intimidated by code, but learn how to speak the
language a little so that I can actually use these tools to build something."*
That is the right starting point. Nobody becomes a programmer in a workshop,
but everyone can learn to direct a capable assistant.

The deck then covers what changed in two and a half years, how to catch up,
and what each of the three sessions builds: a [slidemaker](01_slidemaker/session-1.qmd),
a [document pipeline](02_summarizer/session-2.qmd), and a
[two-agent review](03_multitudes/session-3.qmd). The skill that transfers
between them is the same one: saying clearly what you want, in writing, once.

Ready to start? Do the [setup](session-0.qmd) first.
